correctness.rationale: Theorem 2.2 of arXiv:2311.02920v1 is the finite spanning-tree norm formula. Positive subtree masses permit strict source-to-ancestor and hub-to-root shortcutting; this proves the subset minimum, not just its upper bound. At equal masses, the remaining profile is strictly concave in the routed count; its endpoints give the sharp threshold. Logarithmic expansion proves the support growth. The exhaustive small-tree checker passes 29 comparisons, but the proof covers all finite cardinalities and permitted real parameters.

value.rationale: A natural complete quantitative study of the canonical finite equilateral-plus-hub example behind nonisometric free p-space inclusions: it evaluates every nonnegative single-sink molecule exactly by a subset transport law, proves a necessary-and-sufficient sharp cardinality transition, detects nontrivial selective routing for heterogeneous masses, and identifies exponential support growth as p approaches one. This substantially improves an upper witness and a generic tree-search formula, without claiming a full operator norm or large universal theorem.
